title: Transformer-classified reviews map regional patterns in EV availability discussions
summary: BERT and XLNet classified topics in an archive of 127,257 U.S. charging-station reviews. Spatial analysis placed relatively frequent availability discussions in smaller communities in parts of the West and Midwest, with different patterns in the South and Northeast. The result concerns review-topic frequency, not independently measured charging shortages.
ai_technology: BERT and XLNet supervised topic classification

evidence.tested: The 2011–2015 archive covered 12,720 charging locations and 29,532 users. Human-designed topics were learned from expert-annotated reviews; ten cross-validation runs gave overall accuracy 91.6% and F1 .83/.84 for BERT/XLNet. Predicted topic frequencies were mapped using 2013 metropolitan/micropolitan boundaries and standardized separately into regional quantiles. The source describes smaller-community availability discussion patterns in parts of the West/Midwest and more major-metropolitan patterns in the South/Northeast.
evidence.unknown: Availability is a broad discussion topic encompassing whether stations are available; frequent discussion is not a direct estimate of shortage, station failure or unmet demand. Regional quantile normalization prevents treating the map as a common absolute availability scale. Reviews appear only when users post, do not contain charging transactions and cannot establish population-wide access or causal infrastructure effects. The data were reanalyzed from an existing archive, and topics were manually specified rather than discovered unsupervised. Annotator experts were trained students, not industry professionals; the 100-review audited comparison does not establish universal superhuman annotation. Full supplemental training partitions and spatial counts were not reviewed, so geographic unit-count claims are not reproduced. This represents the January 2021 journal version, despite the 2020 DOI token.
evidence.ai_role: Learned language classifiers scaled manual topic labels across the review corpus, enabling the source-specific spatial analysis. Conventional mapping summarized those learned labels; predicted discussion is kept distinct from observed infrastructure conditions.

source_review.scope: Original primary cohort, learned-model evaluation, represented applied Results, reference labels and bounded limitations actually read; supplementary material not fully assessed.
